summary: A scholar of Indology and linguistics, Burrow studied at Christ's College, Cambridge, SOAS, and Annamalai under E. J. Rapson and P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri. He served at the British Museum, SOAS, and Oxford as Boden Professor of Sanskrit (1944–1976).
Tychsen worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. After studying at Kiel University and the University of Göttingen, he held a post at Göttingen from circa 1784 to 1834.
A scholar in Buddhist studies, sinology, and philosophy, Cleary studied under E. Bruce Brooks, earning a Ph.D. at Harvard University and a JD at the University of California, Berkeley.

Doctor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and the University of Lausanne, working under teachers including Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche, Christian K. Wedemeyer, and doctoral supervisor Tom Tillemans.

Crow studied at Pomona College and UCLA. He taught at CalArts, Chicago, Princeton, Michigan, Sussex, Yale, and USC, served as director of the Getty Research Institute (2000–2007), and was appointed Rosalie Solow Professor of Modern Art at NYU in 2007.

Colebrooke studied at Eton College and East India Company College. Active in Indology, he served as President (1864–1882) and Vice-President (until 1890) of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

Yarnall is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Educated at the University of Washington and Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman, he served as Executive Editor in Columbia's Department of Religion (attested 2007).
Huxley studied at Great Ealing School, Charing Cross Hospital Medical School, UCL, and Imperial College School of Medicine. He held a post at Imperial College London from circa 1854 to 1885.

A scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies, Mazanec studied at Calvin University and the University of Colorado, completing doctoral work under supervisors Anna M. Shields and Stephen F. Teiser, and doctoral advisor Wang Ping.

Jülch is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Goethe University Frankfurt, University of Hull, Heidelberg University, and University of Munich (PhD), later working as a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University (2013–2019).
Specializing in Buddhist and religious studies, Patton earned his PhD at Cornell University under Anne M. Blackburn. He held a post at the City University of Hong Kong (attested 2018).
Working in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies, Oberlies studied under Paul Thieme and Albrecht Wezler, and held a post at the University of Freiburg (attested 2001).
Specializing in philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology, Kasulis held posts at Ashland University (circa 1980–1991) and Ohio State University, where he was a professor from circa 1991 to 2018.

Trautmann is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham and held a post as professor for history and anthropology at the University of Michigan (attested 1991).
Malthus studied at Warrington Academy and the University of Cambridge, including Jesus College, Cambridge.

A scholar of linguistics and Indology, Roebuck studied at the Royal High School, Edinburgh. He was a member of The Asiatic Society (circa 1810–1819) and assistant-secretary and examiner at the College of Fort St George in 1811.
Watters, a scholar in sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, earned a B.A. studying at Queen's University Belfast and Queen's University of Ireland from 1857 to 1861.
Zehnder works in Indology and linguistics. He earned his PhD at the University of Zurich under supervisor Alexander Lubotsky.

A Buddhist studies scholar, Chodron studied at UCLA, USC, Kopan, and Dorje Pamo. She held posts at Istituto Lama Tzong Khapa, Amitabha Buddhist Centre, and Dharma Friendship Foundation, and founded Sravasti Abbey in 2003, serving as its abbess.
Gyatso worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Agvan Dorzhiev and held a post at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center (attested 1988).
